name: The Vedda Ford
description: The old crossing, downstream of everything, still the shallowest water.
arrival: Shingle on both banks and a bar between them you can wade at low water. There are stones set in the bed that are not river stones, worn round, laid a pace apart.
notes:
**The oldest of three crossings, and the one still in use.** The Vedda forded here in `epoch_migrations`, the Age of Machinery bridged it, and the nomads ford it again -- the same water, because water does not care what anybody builds.

The player finds them in the wrong order: the rail-head first, this last. That is what makes the rail sad rather than impressive. It is the middle of three things, not the end of one.
